scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: On every 16-line union of the coordinate frame with one of the 1260 complementary E8 frames, what is the exact copied-information cost of an eight-term ordinary-transpose factorization of 2G, and does the even-entry mask lower that cost when the coordinate readers stay fixed?
scope_change_reason: The card's first experiment is one finite support alphabet before a network. These 16 lines are the frame-pair puncture, taken as the live alphabet rather than as a p<=24 complement. The eight-term complement search is not repeated. No complete moment is formed because the copy ratio 1 is coarser than 7/13 and restoration is not priced.
bottleneck_link: The binding complex supplier is limited by decoder copy cost. This alphabet is the equality-case puncture of the eight-term floor, so its own exact charge shows whether masking those lines beats the complement ratio. It does not: eight terms cost 16 on 16 lines, and fixed coordinate readers have the same charge under the even mask.
stop_rule: Stop after the eight-term identity and lower bound on this alphabet, including the fixed-reader mask. Do not search longer factorizations or build a hosted word in this session.
